messages:
Sam L: quick heads-up — I ran the split-flow experiment (silo prefill vs decode) on staging with the epoch scheduler tweak.
Anya R: nice, what metrics looked off?
Sam L: p95 latency jumped ~12% on small seq workloads, throughput steady. perf-ci logged a kernel fallback rate increase.
perf-ci: perf report: p50 48ms -> 52ms, p95 210ms -> 235ms, kernel_fallback_rate +18%, kv-miss-rate +6% :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Kevin T: can you paste the config you used? guessing token_budget targets or queue aging caused more decode spillover.
Sam L: config snippet:
```
epoch_scheduler:
  epoch_ms: 8
  prefill_batch_max_tokens: 2048
  decode_batch_max_tokens: 1024
  token_budget_target: 1200
queue_policy:
  prefer_prefill: false
  decode_priority_boost: 0.15
  kv_warmup_threshold_ms: 30
```
Jia W: curious why `prefer_prefill: false` — that can let decode steal kernels mid-cycle, forcing kernel selection to prefer decode paths and evict some cached KV shards.
Sam L: agreed — I flipped it to test handoff fairness. The idea was to reduce prefill tail by splitting, but seems to introduce more kernel thrash and KV cold starts.
Anya R: did you run kernel-selector traces? want to know if we went from fp16-optimized kernels to fallback int8 paths.
perf-ci: kernel trace attached: selector chose fallback for 14% of decode batches after handoff. fallback reason: "gemm tile mismatch" and "workspace insuf".
Kevin T: that smells like batch shape churn. If decode batches are smaller and more numerous after separation, selector prefers conservative kernels. Need grouping by sequence length when forming batches.
Sam L: I tried grouping by `seq_bucket` but our continuous batcher uses token_budget to fill across phase-boundaries which might be mixing seq lengths.
Jia W: thoughts: add a phase-aware token budget allocator — reserve X% tokens for prefill per epoch, let decode use leftover. That should reduce decode-first fill that breaks kernel packing.
Anya R: +1. Also suggest we add a short KV-pin window: keep recently used KV shards pinned for N epochs after prefill to avoid immediate eviction when decode hot-swaps.
Kevin T: small change proposal:
```
phase_token_alloc:
  prefill_pct: 0.65
  decode_pct: 0.35
kv_pin_epochs: 2
batch_packing:
  group_by: [model, seq_bucket]
  prefer_kernel: "fp16_fast"
```
Sam L: I'll run a 6-hour canary with those settings. expectation: fallback rate down, p95 back to baseline, maybe slight throughput dip but overall better latency SLO.
perf-ci: scheduling canary queued — will post metrics after 2h and 6h :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Jia W: if canary looks good, we should consider changing default queue policy to prefer prefill in mixed workloads. For enterprise customers with latency SLOs, decode stealing is high risk.
Anya R: also add an eval set that stresses short seq chat-style sessions to catch this early in CI.
Sam L: good call. I'll add a quick eval harness that simulates 1-8 token decodes interleaved with 200-512 token prefill requests.
deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: staging->canary-split-flow at 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z
Sam L: thanks. will update thread with perf graphs and kernel selector logs once available.
Anya R: thx — if you see kv-miss spike >10% revert `prefer_prefill` immediately.
Sam L: noted. :eyes:
